submission.natural_language_explanation: Retrospective: the pole peaks on the clause-linking word itself - concessive subordinators (although, while, whereas), result connectives (therefore, thus, consequently, meanwhile), the relative/comparative functors which, than and like, and the constative relational predicates (is called, uses, contains, involves, located, means) - when that word opens a clause after a full stop or a comma. It stays near zero on the additive/contrastive adverbials however, moreover, furthermore, nevertheless and nonetheless, on the causal subordinators because and since, on plain sentence openers (In, For, Some, These, The) and on concrete content nouns.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: IN THE MATTER OF THE HARBOR LIGHT EASEMENT. The hearing convened on the morning of March third in the assembly room of the county offices. The commissioners sat behind a long oak table, and the clerk read the notice into the record. Counsel for the harbor authority described the history of the disputed right of way. The path begins at the old lighthouse and follows the shoreline for nearly a mile before turning inland toward the salt marsh. Fishermen used the path for generations, and the authority maintains that public access has never been interrupted. The landowners disagree. Their attorney presented a stack of deeds and tax records stretching back to the nineteenth century. He argued that the path crossed private ground and that the public had no right to pass. Several residents testified about the winter storms that washed out the lower section of the trail. The surveyor's report, filed in February, notes that the eastern bank has eroded by nearly twelve feet. The report also describes the condition of the wooden footbridge. Two of its planks are missing, and the railing has pulled loose from the posts. The harbor authority proposes to rebuild the bridge and reinforce the bank with stone. The landowners object to the cost and to the increased traffic. They also question whether the authority owns the underlying land. The commissioners listened to both sides for several hours. They asked about the wording of the original grant, the maintenance records, and the public use of the path during the last fifty years. A retired teacher described walking the path as a child. A lobsterman described using it to reach his traps after a storm. The clerk entered photographs and maps into the record. The hearing resumed after lunch, and the discussion turned to the language of the 1874 deed. The deed describes a right of way for all persons passing along the shore. The landowners' attorney focused on the word passing. He argued that it covered travel on foot only, and not the vehicles that the authority now permits. The authority's attorney replied that the deed was written long before motor vehicles existed and that the intent was to preserve public access. The commissioners asked for a short recess. When they returned, the chair announced that the panel would visit the site before issuing a decision. The clerk scheduled the inspection for the following week. An engineer from the state coastal office explained how the tide had shifted the channel over the decades. She recommended a new survey before any construction begins and noted that the authority's budget already includes a line for the survey. The county clerk confirmed that all exhibits had been copied and distributed to both parties. The record includes the 1874 deed, the 1891 easement, and the surveyor's February report. The easement had been recorded in 1891. Though the landowners disputed its scope, the commissioners found the original grant unambiguous. The hearing closed at four o'clock, and the record remained open for written comments until the end of the month. A final decision is expected in April, and the clerk will notify both parties by mail.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Hypothesis predicts activation: concessive 'Though' opens a clause after a full stop deep inside a 500-plus-word legal-hearing passage from a different genre, testing class generalization and long-context stability.
